description: MIC Length selector (LLSec bits 2-4) semantics test vectors per spec/02-physical-link.md section 4.2. Spec says: '0 or 1=compatibility selector; 2-7=reserved'. This file tests the difference (if any) between selector values 0 and 1.
oracle_provenance: Independent analysis of spec text. The spec does not define any behavioral difference between selector 0 and selector 1 - both result in no MIC when signature_present=false, or 48-byte Schnorr signature when signature_present=true.

clarification.selector_0_behavior: No MIC field (0 bytes) when signature_present=false; 48-byte Schnorr when signature_present=true
clarification.selector_1_behavior: Identical to selector 0 in current spec. Reserved for future compatibility if MIC format changes.
clarification.rationale: The 'compatibility selector' mechanism allows future protocol versions to signal a different MIC format. Current implementations MUST treat 0 and 1 identically.

vectors.name: mic_length_0_unsigned
vectors.description: MIC selector 0, signature_present=false: no MIC field

vectors.name: mic_length_1_unsigned
vectors.description: MIC selector 1, signature_present=false: no MIC field (identical to selector 0)

expected.note: Selector 1 behaves identically to selector 0 per spec

vectors.name: mic_length_0_signed
vectors.description: MIC selector 0 with signature_present=true: 48-byte Schnorr signature

vectors.name: mic_length_1_signed
vectors.description: MIC selector 1 with signature_present=true: 48-byte Schnorr signature (identical to selector 0)

expected.note: Selector 1 behaves identically to selector 0 per spec

vectors.name: mic_length_2_reserved_reject
vectors.description: MIC selector 2 is reserved: MUST reject

vectors.name: mic_length_3_reserved_reject
vectors.description: MIC selector 3 is reserved: MUST reject

vectors.name: mic_length_7_reserved_reject
vectors.description: MIC selector 7 (max value) is reserved: MUST reject

vectors.name: selector_1_with_short_addr
vectors.description: MIC selector 1 with 16-bit address, unsigned (identical behavior to selector 0)

vectors.name: selector_1_with_extended_addr
vectors.description: MIC selector 1 with 64-bit address, unsigned (identical behavior)
